I have farmed here in Quzhou County for 20 years. I never went to school, but I know every corner of my 349.9 mu. There are four of us in the household, and we rely on our well for water when the rain is not enough. Sweetpotato is our main cropping system — that is what this family farm was built around, and the starch factory in town buys them steady. I will plant 130 mu of sweetpotato again this year, starting around May 1. I buy improved seed tubers — about 2,750 plants per mu. I will rotary-till the land, broadcast 60 jin of general compound fertilizer and 25 jin of potassium sulphate as basal dressing, and topdress twice when the tubers start swelling. I will irrigate twice from the well, and spray twice for insects, once for weeds, and three times with growth regulator to keep the vines from running wild. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

For maize, I will plant 150 mu with nongda372 hybrid seed. It is reliable and the grain station always takes it. I will rotary-till and put down 80 jin per mu of special high-nitrogen compound fertilizer as basal. Maize does not need much irrigation here — once from the well is usually enough. I will spray twice for insects, once for weeds, and once with growth regulator. I expect 1,000 jin per mu.

The remaining 69.9 mu goes to millet — huangjingu variety. Millet is tough and does not need much water, so one irrigation is plenty. I will rotary-till and use 75 jin per mu of general compound fertilizer. I will spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I expect about 350 jin per mu, and the price is better than maize.
